newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain won't miss EMU train - Aznar.
newsitem.headline: Spain won't miss EMU train - Aznar.

text.p: Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said on Friday he was convinced Spain could buck a historical trend and not "miss the train" to European Monetary Union.

Despite reservations expressed by some European central bankers lately over a wider union that would include countries like Spain and Italy from the start, Aznar said he was "absolutely convinced of Spain's ability" to qualify.
He hoped to "constitute an exception to our history -- instead of missing the train, we will catch it on time."
Spain is hoping a restrictive 1997 budget, which the government has presented to parliament will put the economy in shape to meet the Maastricht treaty convergency criteria.
Aznar is determined to position Spain among the the first round of countries joining the single currency launch set for 1999.
But some European central bankers have expressed reservations about countries with more volatile economies joining the monetary union immediately.
